youtube.aciklama:
Four important syndromes with hearing loss: long QT and congenital severe loss in Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome, conductive loss and bone conduction devices in Treacher Collins syndrome, semicircular canal anomalies in CHARGE syndrome, and middle ear fluid and hearing monitoring in Down syndrome.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: GeneReviews: Jervell and Lange-Nielsen Syndrome, Treacher Collins Syndrome, CHD7 Disorder; MedlinePlus Genetics; Bull et al., Health Supervision for Children and Adolescents With Down Syndrome (Pediatrics, 2022); Katz, Handbook of Clinical Audiology.

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

sahneler.alt: JLNS, Treacher Collins, CHARGE and Down
cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.
In this lesson we will learn four more syndromes with hearing loss: Jervell and Lange-Nielsen, Treacher Collins, CHARGE and Down syndrome.
For each one, we will cover the main features, the type of hearing loss, and key points for audiological monitoring.
Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome, or JLNS, is a syndrome that affects hearing and the heart together.
It is autosomal recessive and quite rare; its reported prevalence is about one point six to six per million.
The hearing loss is congenital, bilateral, and severe to profound sensorineural.
In the heart, the electrocardiogram shows a long QT interval.
The corrected QT interval is often longer than five hundred milliseconds.
Long QT sets the stage for rhythm disorders that can cause fainting and sudden death with exercise, excitement or fear.

cumleler.yazi: Most cases have variants in both copies of the KCNQ1 gene, and fewer in both copies of KCNE1.
cumleler.ses: Most cases have variants in both copies of the K C N Q 1 gene, and fewer in both copies of K C N E 1.

cumleler.yazi: The syndrome was first described in 1957 in Norway by Jervell and Lange-Nielsen.
cumleler.ses: The syndrome was first described in nineteen fifty seven in Norway by Jervell and Lange-Nielsen.

sahneler.baslik: *The same channel* in ear and heart
cumleler: We can understand why the ear and heart are affected together through the potassium cycle we saw in the genetics lessons.

cumleler.yazi: The KCNQ1 and KCNE1 genes encode two proteins that together form a potassium channel.
cumleler.ses: The K C N Q 1 and K C N E 1 genes encode two proteins that together form a potassium channel.

cumleler: This channel is part of the system in the cells of the stria vascularis that pumps potassium into the endolymph.
When the channel fails, not enough endolymph is produced, and the environment cochlear hair cells need to work is not formed.
The same channel helps heart muscle cells return to their resting state after each beat.
When the channel is faulty, this return is prolonged, and it appears on the electrocardiogram as a long QT interval.

sahneler.baslik: JLNS: what it *means* for the audiologist
cumleler: JLNS is rare, but it should come to mind in every child with congenital severe hearing loss.
Fainting with exercise or excitement, events mistaken for seizures, and sudden death at a young age in the family are especially important.
So many etiologic workup protocols include an electrocardiogram for children with congenital severe loss.
The electrocardiogram and treatment decisions belong to the physician; the audiologist's task is to notice and pass on warning signs.
For a child planned for a sedated brainstem response test or a cochlear implant, the team knowing this diagnosis matters for safety.
Cochlear implants usually give good hearing outcomes in children with JLNS; cardiac follow-up continues for life.
Treacher Collins syndrome affects the development of the face and the ear.
It occurs in about one in fifty thousand births.
The cheekbones and lower jaw are underdeveloped, which gives the face a typical appearance.
The eye openings slant outward and downward; there may be a notch in the lower eyelid or missing lashes.
The auricle may be small or malformed; the ear canal may be narrow or not developed at all, that is, atretic.

cumleler.yazi: In most cases, inheritance is autosomal dominant, with a variant in the TCOF1 gene.
cumleler.ses: In most cases, inheritance is autosomal dominant, with a variant in the T C O F 1 gene.

cumleler.yazi: Less often, the POLR1D, POLR1C and POLR1B genes are responsible; the POLR1C related form is recessive.
cumleler.ses: Less often, the P O L R 1 D, P O L R 1 C and P O L R 1 B genes are responsible; the P O L R 1 C related form is recessive.

cumleler: A large share of cases appear for the first time in a family, from a new variant.
Even within one family, the severity of the features can vary greatly.
Intellectual development is usually normal, so early support for hearing is very important for language development.
In Treacher Collins syndrome, hearing loss is often bilateral and conductive; sources report it in about half of cases.
In this example audiogram, air conduction thresholds in both ears are between fifty and sixty decibels HL.
Bone conduction thresholds are within normal limits, so the inner ear is working, and the difference is a large air-bone gap.
The loss comes from ear canal atresia and malformations of the ossicular chain.
A large bilateral conductive loss can create a masking dilemma, and an insert earphone cannot be placed in an atretic ear.
So electrophysiological tests such as bone conduction auditory brainstem response, or ABR, give important ear-specific support.
If a loss is suspected in the newborn period, inner ear function is assessed with bone conduction ABR, even if the ear canal is closed.
Since the inner ear is usually normal, delivering sound to the cochlea by bone conduction is the most natural solution.
In young children, a bone conduction hearing device is usually worn on the head with an elastic softband.
Device choice and timing are planned within the team, based on the child's ear and facial anatomy.
Speech and language therapy starts early; since cognition is normal, good auditory access can support language development.
The timing of ear and facial surgery is decided by the relevant physicians and the team.

ogeler.metin: A tissue gap in the eye

cumleler: CHARGE syndrome takes its name from the initials of its most common features.
C is coloboma, a congenital gap in the tissue of the eye that can affect vision.
H stands for heart disease, and A for atresia of the choanae, a closed or narrow opening at the back of the nose.
R stands for retardation of growth and development, and G for genital underdevelopment.
E stands for ear anomalies and hearing loss; for the audiologist, it is the most important letter.

cumleler.yazi: The syndrome occurs in about one in ten to seventeen thousand births; most cases have a new variant in the CHD7 gene.
cumleler.ses: The syndrome occurs in about one in ten to seventeen thousand births; most cases have a new variant in the C H D 7 gene.

cumleler: The diagnosis rests on a combination of these features; not every child has every letter.
In CHARGE syndrome, every part of the ear can be affected.
The auricle may be short and wide, with a small or absent lobe; this appearance is an important diagnostic clue.
The most characteristic inner ear finding is underdeveloped or absent semicircular canals.

cumleler.yazi: This finding is seen on imaging in the great majority of children with a CHD7 variant.
cumleler.ses: This finding is seen on imaging in the great majority of children with a C H D 7 variant.

cumleler: So vestibular function is often markedly reduced; head control, sitting and walking may be delayed.
Hearing loss ranges from mild to profound and is often mixed; the auditory nerve may also be underdeveloped.
Because the auditory nerve may be underdeveloped, imaging the nerve is important when a cochlear implant is considered.
If coloboma also affects vision, the child has losses in two senses at once, and the communication plan is built around this.
Behavioral tests such as visual reinforcement audiometry, which we will see later, are adapted to the child's vision and motor status.
In the pediatric assessment section, we will look at these adaptations in detail for children with multiple disabilities.
Middle ear fluid is also common, so tympanometry and the conductive component are monitored regularly.
Swallowing and feeding problems are also common, so appointments are planned by the team along with the child's other care needs.

maddeler.metin: Middle ear fluid is very common
Narrow ear canals: hard to examine

cumleler: Down syndrome results from an extra copy of chromosome twenty one and is the most common chromosomal difference.
Hearing loss is common in these children; the most common cause is long-lasting middle ear fluid, as we saw in the Eustachian tube lesson.
The ear canals are often narrow, which makes otoscopy, tympanometry and earwax removal harder.
An adult probe tip may not seal well in a narrow canal; a tip of the right size must be chosen.
Besides conductive losses, sensorineural and mixed losses are also more common than in the general population.
Age-related hearing loss is reported to start earlier in adulthood, so monitoring continues for life.
Even when the loss is mild, its impact is large in a child whose language development already needs support.

cumleler.yazi: The 2022 American Academy of Pediatrics guideline advises close hearing monitoring in Down syndrome; the first step is newborn screening.
cumleler.ses: The twenty twenty two American Academy of Pediatrics guideline advises close hearing monitoring in Down syndrome; the first step is newborn screening.

cumleler: In infancy and the preschool years, tympanometry and behavioral audiometry are repeated about every six months.
This frequent monitoring continues until ear-specific testing shows normal hearing in both ears, often after age four.
After that, hearing is assessed once a year through school age and adolescence.
Behavioral tests for these children are chosen by developmental age; the response expected for chronological age may not come.
Because middle ear fluid causes fluctuating loss, a single normal result is not enough to end monitoring.
If an ear canal is very narrow and blocked with wax, referral to a physician for cleaning is a routine part of monitoring.

sahneler.metin: In a child with congenital severe loss, ask about fainting and sudden deaths at a young age in the family; pass the finding to the physician.
cumleler: A tip from the clinic: recognizing syndromes often means looking beyond the ear.
Ask the family of a child with congenital severe loss about fainting with exercise or excitement, and early sudden deaths in the family.
Add your observations on facial structure, the eyes, the heart and motor development to the report.
This information is valuable for genetic assessment and medical referral; the diagnosis belongs to the physician and genetics team.

maddeler.metin: JLNS: congenital severe loss and _long QT_
Down: middle ear fluid, close monitoring

cumleler: Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome is autosomal recessive; congenital severe sensorineural loss comes with long QT.
In Treacher Collins syndrome, the facial bones and ear are affected; the loss is mostly bilateral and conductive.
CHARGE syndrome can show mixed loss, underdeveloped semicircular canals and auditory nerve anomalies.
In Down syndrome, middle ear fluid and narrow ear canals are common; hearing is monitored at regular intervals.

sahneler.soru: Which syndrome comes with long QT?
sahneler.aciklama: _The same potassium channel_ is affected in the ear and the heart.

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: which syndrome combines congenital severe hearing loss with a long QT interval?

cumleler: The correct answer is B: Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome.

cumleler.yazi: The potassium channel encoded by KCNQ1 and KCNE1 works both in the stria vascularis and in heart muscle.
cumleler.ses: The potassium channel encoded by K C N Q 1 and K C N E 1 works both in the stria vascularis and in heart muscle.
